glance_notes.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Voting in Hawaii
glance_notes.text: Hawaii Elections Are Conducted by Mail: Hawaii conducts its elections by mail. Every properly registered voter automatically receives a mail ballot approximately 18 days before the election. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voters are expected to receive their ballots by October 16.

Same-Day Registration Available: Hawaii provides same-day voter registration at voter service centers. For the 2026 General Election, voter service centers operate from October 20 through November 3, excluding Sundays, with locations and hours established by the County Elections Divisions.

glance_notes.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Elections in Hawaii
glance_notes.text: Ballots Must Be Received by 7:00 p.m.: Completed ballots for the November 3, 2026 General Election must be received by the appropriate County Elections Division by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. A postmark does not satisfy the deadline.

register.label: Register to Vote
register.content: Eligible Hawaii residents can register online, submit a paper Voter Registration Application, register through the Department of Motor Vehicles or designated public-assistance agencies, or register in person at a voter service center. To register, you must be a U.S. citizen, be a resident of Hawaii with the intent to make Hawaii your legal residence, and be at least 18 years old to vote. Hawaii permits eligible individuals to preregister beginning at age 16. Online registration requires a Hawaii driver license or Hawaii State ID and a Social Security number. Once properly registered, a voter automatically receives a ballot by mail for each election.
register.glance_value: Online, paper, DMV or same-day registration
register.internal_note: Official source directly establishes citizenship, residency, age and preregistration qualifications; online and paper registration; automatic voter registration through DMV; public-assistance agency registration; and same-day registration. Online registration portal: [https://olvr.hawaii.gov/](https://olvr.hawaii.gov/). The Office of Elections expressly states that presence in Hawaii alone does not establish voting residence; the applicant must intend to make Hawaii the person's legal residence.

check_registration.label: Check Voter Registration
check_registration.content: Hawaii voters can check and update their voter registration through the state's Online Voter Registration system. Online access requires a Hawaii driver license or Hawaii State ID and the last four digits of the voter's Social Security number. Voters may also contact their County Elections Division to confirm registration status or obtain proof of registration.
check_registration.glance_value: Check online or with your county
check_registration.source_name: State of Hawaii — Online Voter Registration System
check_registration.internal_note: Hawaii Office of Elections Registration — [https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/) — directly confirms online verification requirements and states that County Elections Divisions manage voter records and can confirm registration or provide proof of registration.

deadlines.label: Registration Deadlines
deadlines.content: For the November 3, 2026 General Election, paper Voter Registration Applications must be submitted to the appropriate County Elections Division by 4:30 p.m. on October 26, 2026. Hawaii's online voter registration system remains available after the paper deadline, and eligible voters may also register and vote in person through same-day registration at a voter service center through Election Day.
deadlines.glance_value: Paper deadline October 26; same-day registration available
deadlines.internal_note: The Office of Elections directly establishes October 26, 2026 as the paper registration deadline and states that online registration is available at any time. It also directly establishes same-day registration at voter service centers beginning 10 days before the election and continuing through Election Day. The statewide 2026 election information lists General Election voter service centers from October 20 through November 3, excluding Sundays.

polling_place.label: Find a Voting Location
polling_place.content: Hawaii conducts elections primarily by mail rather than through traditional assigned Election Day polling places. Voters who want or need to vote in person may use a voter service center operated by their County Elections Division. Voter service centers provide in-person voting, same-day registration and accessible voting. The Office of Elections publishes the official voter service center locations and ballot drop boxes for each county.
polling_place.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Voter Service Centers and Ballot Drop Boxes
polling_place.internal_note: Hawaii's 2026 Proclamation establishes that the elections are conducted by mail and publishes county-specific voter service centers and places of deposit. The statewide voter service center page contains the official 2026 locations and operating schedules.

election_day.label: Election Day Voting
election_day.content: Hawaii's November 3, 2026 General Election is conducted primarily by mail. Voters who choose or need to vote in person may use a voter service center. On Election Day, regular voter service centers are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Voters may register or update their registration and vote in person at a voter service center. Completed mail ballots must be received by the appropriate County Elections Division by 7:00 p.m. on Election Day.
election_day.glance_value: Voter service centers open until 7 p.m.
election_day.internal_note: The 2026 Proclamation directly establishes the General Election date and Election Day voter service center hours. Hawaii Office of Elections Elections in Hawaii — [https://elections.hawaii.gov/elections-in-hawaii/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/elections-in-hawaii/) — establishes the 7:00 p.m. ballot receipt deadline and same-day registration availability.

polling_hours.label: Voting Hours
polling_hours.content: Hawaii does not use traditional statewide Election Day polling places because elections are conducted by mail. On November 3, 2026, regular voter service centers are open from 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. Ballots returned to election officials or ballot drop boxes must be received by 7:00 p.m. Exact pre-Election Day voter service center hours vary by county and location.
polling_hours.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Voter Service Centers and Ballot Drop Boxes
polling_hours.internal_note: Official 2026 county schedules show regular voter service centers operating 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Pre-election hours differ among counties and some additional locations operate for shorter periods, so no single statewide pre-election daily schedule should be stated.

early_voting.label: Early In-Person Voting
early_voting.content: Although Hawaii conducts elections by mail, voters may vote in person before Election Day at voter service centers. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voter service centers are available beginning October 20 and continuing through November 3, excluding Sundays. Regular pre-Election Day hours are generally Monday through Saturday, but exact hours and additional temporary locations vary by county. Voter service centers also provide same-day registration and accessible voting.
early_voting.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Elections in Hawaii
early_voting.internal_note: The Office of Elections directly identifies October 20-November 3, excluding Sundays, as the statewide 2026 General Election voter service center period. Detailed official locations and hours: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/). The 2026 Proclamation confirms county-specific schedules and additional temporary sites. This is functionally Hawaii's in-person early-voting option, but the state's terminology is 'voter service centers.'

absentee_mail.label: Mail & Absentee Voting
absentee_mail.content: Hawaii conducts elections by mail. Every properly registered voter automatically receives a mail ballot approximately 18 days before each election, so voters do not need to request a standard ballot. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, voters are expected to receive their ballots by October 16. A voter who needs a ballot mailed to an alternate address must submit an absentee application to the appropriate County Elections Division by October 27. Completed ballots may be returned by mail or delivered to an authorized ballot drop box or election location, but they must be received by the County Elections Division no later than 7:00 p.m. on Election Day. Postmarks do not extend the deadline.
absentee_mail.glance_value: Ballots automatically mailed to registered voters
absentee_mail.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Voting in Hawaii
absentee_mail.internal_note: Primary source establishes automatic ballot mailing approximately 18 days before elections. Current statewide 2026 information establishes October 16 as the General Election ballot-arrival date, October 27 as the alternate-address request deadline, and 7:00 p.m. November 3 as the receipt deadline. The Office of Elections has repeatedly warned that ballots must be received, not merely postmarked, by the deadline. Official drop-box information: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/).

voter_id.label: Voter ID Requirements
voter_id.content: Because Hawaii automatically mails ballots to registered voters, most voters casting their regular ballot by mail do not present identification at a voting location. Identity information is used during registration and election administration, and a voter using Hawaii's online registration system must provide a Hawaii driver license or Hawaii State ID and Social Security number. Voters appearing at a voter service center should follow the identification and verification instructions provided by election officials, particularly when registering or updating a registration in person.
voter_id.glance_value: No routine photo ID presentation for mailed ballots
voter_id.internal_note: Hawaii's current official voter materials emphasize identity verification through voter registration and ballot-signature procedures rather than a conventional Election Day photo-ID requirement. The registration page establishes the Hawaii driver license/Hawaii State ID and Social Security number requirements for online registration. Because same-day registrants and individual voter circumstances can trigger additional verification procedures, the reader-facing content avoids making an unsupported categorical claim that identification can never be requested at a voter service center.

accessible_voting.label: Accessible Voting
accessible_voting.content: Hawaii provides several accessible voting options. Every registered voter receives a paper mail ballot that can be completed at home. Voters with special needs may request an accessible electronic ballot from their County Elections Division, download and mark it privately using compatible assistive technology, and return it using the methods authorized by the state. Voter service centers are equipped with accessible ballot-marking devices. A voter who needs assistance because of a disability, visual or hearing impairment, or inability to read or write may also receive help from a person of the voter's choice, except the voter's employer, an agent of the employer or an agent of the voter's union.
accessible_voting.glance_value: Accessible mail, electronic and in-person voting
accessible_voting.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Voter Accessibility
accessible_voting.internal_note: The official accessibility page was updated April 23, 2026 and directly establishes accessible electronic ballots, voter service center ballot-marking equipment and voter assistance rights. Hawaii specifically identifies the Verity Touch Writer as the accessible ballot-marking device at voter service centers.

military_overseas.label: Military & Overseas Voting
military_overseas.content: Hawaii military and overseas voters covered by federal law may use the Federal Post Card Application to register and request a ballot. Uniformed-service members, eligible family members and qualified U.S. citizens living outside the United States may receive election materials at an eligible alternate address and use federal military and overseas voting procedures. The Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot is available as a backup for eligible voters when necessary. Military and overseas voters should submit requests early and follow the current return instructions from their County Elections Division because delivery and return options can differ from the standard Hawaii mail-ballot process.
military_overseas.glance_value: FPCA and federal overseas voting protections available
military_overseas.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Military and Overseas Voters
military_overseas.internal_note: Hawaii Office of Elections Registration — [https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/) — expressly states that uniformed and overseas citizens whose last residence was in Hawaii may use the FPCA to register and simultaneously request a ballot at an out-of-state address. The dedicated military and overseas page provides UOCAVA resources and service voting-assistance contacts. Federal forms and specific return procedures should be checked for the individual voter's circumstances rather than summarized beyond what Hawaii's current official guidance affirmatively establishes.

student_voting.label: College / Student Voting
student_voting.content: A Hawaii resident attending college outside the state may remain registered in Hawaii and request that the Hawaii ballot be mailed to the student's current college address. A Hawaii resident attending college within the state may likewise request delivery to a campus address. The student must submit an absentee application each election year that the student is away from the Hawaii residence. For the November 3, 2026 General Election, the deadline for the County Elections Division to receive an absentee application requesting delivery to an alternate address is October 27.
student_voting.glance_value: Students can request delivery to a college address
student_voting.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — College Students
student_voting.internal_note: The current official College Students page directly establishes procedures for Hawaii residents attending either out-of-state or in-state colleges, the requirement to submit an absentee application each election year when away from the Hawaii residence, and the October 27, 2026 General Election deadline. This section deliberately does not infer that attendance at a Hawaii college by a nonresident automatically establishes Hawaii voting residence.

sample_ballot.label: Official Voter Guide & Ballot Information
sample_ballot.content: The Hawaii Office of Elections publishes official voter guides and election information to help voters review candidates and ballot questions before voting. Ballot contents depend on the voter's residence and districts. Use the Office of Elections voter resources and voter guide for the current General Election materials as they become available.
sample_ballot.flagged_reason: The Office of Elections currently provides the 2026 Primary Election voter guide, but a finalized 2026 General Election voter guide or voter-specific General Election sample ballot was not confirmed on the official site when verified.
sample_ballot.internal_note: The Office of Elections homepage currently links the 2026 Primary Election Voter Guide. The November 3 General Election is established and candidate qualification is underway/completed as applicable, but the official General Election voter guide should be rechecked after publication. Do not imply that the Primary guide is the General Election ballot.

contact.label: Contact the State Election Authority
contact.content: Hawaii Office of Elections, 802 Lehua Avenue, Pearl City, HI 96782. Phone: 808-453-VOTE (8683). Neighbor Island toll-free: 1-800-442-VOTE (8683). TTY: 808-453-6150. TTY toll-free: 1-800-345-5915. Fax: 808-453-6006. Email: elections@hawaii.gov. Business hours are 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday through Friday, except state holidays. Questions about individual voter registration, ballot mailing or receipt, replacement ballots, voter service centers and ballot drop boxes should be directed to the voter's County Elections Division.
contact.source_name: Hawaii Office of Elections — Contact Us
contact.internal_note: The Office of Elections contact page directly verifies the address, phone, toll-free number, TTY numbers, fax and hours. Its web-rendered email is protected in search output, but the literal [elections@hawaii.gov](mailto:elections@hawaii.gov) address is independently printed in the Office of Elections official Candidate's Manual hosted at [https://elections.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024-Candidates-Manual.pdf](https://elections.hawaii.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024-Candidates-Manual.pdf). Email is intentionally plain text in content, with no Markdown or mailto wrapper.

official_resources.label: Official State & County Resources
official_resources.content: Use the Hawaii Office of Elections website for statewide election information and the Online Voter Registration system to register, check or update a registration. Hawaii's County Elections Divisions administer voter registration records, ballot mailing and receipt, replacement ballots, voter service centers and ballot drop boxes. County election offices serve the County of Hawaii, County of Maui, County of Kauai, and City and County of Honolulu.
official_resources.glance_value: Office of Elections & County Elections Divisions
official_resources.internal_note: Official online registration: [https://olvr.hawaii.gov/](https://olvr.hawaii.gov/). Official registration guidance: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/register-to-vote/registration/). Official 2026 election information: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/elections-in-hawaii/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/elections-in-hawaii/). Official voter service centers and drop boxes: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/voter-service-centers-and-places-of-deposit/). Official contact page: [https://elections.hawaii.gov/about-us/contact-us/](https://elections.hawaii.gov/about-us/contact-us/). All URLs in this record are bare URL strings; no Markdown hyperlink syntax is used.
